senses.gloss: (b. h.) also Nif. נִגַּשׁ to come in contact; to draw near.
units: <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 842:7">Yalk. Ps. 842</cite> (ref. to <he>יגש</he>, <cite ref="Psalms 91:7">Ps. XCI, 7</cite>) <he>אין אחד מהם נִגָּשׁ אליך וכ׳</he> none of them comes to thee, none says, provide for me; <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 17:7">Midr. Till. to Ps. XVII, 7</cite> <he>נוֹגֵשׁ אצלך</he> ed. Bub. (oth. ed. <he>נוֹגֵשׂ אותך</he>, v. <cite ref="N00196"><he>נָגַשׂ</he></cite>).—Tanḥ. Vayigg. 5 (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 44:18">Gen. XLIV, 18</cite>) <he>שנ׳ בתוכחות</he> he came near (attacked him, v. <cite ref="N00195">next w.</cite>) with rebukes.
Yalk. Gen. 150 (ref. to Gen. l. c.) אין וַיִּגַּשׁ אלא לשון שלום vayyigash has the meaning of (coming near in) peacefulness &c., v. הַגָּשָׁה.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 46b:5">B. Kam. 46ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 24:14">Ex. XXIV, 14</cite>) <he>יַגִּישׁ ראיה אליהם</he> (a claimant) must offer evidence &c.; <he>יגיש דבריו וכ׳</he> must prefer his claims &c., is the first to be heard; a. e.
